***** **
 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents seeking compensation on account of death of the deceased Sri.Aqeeb @ Aqeeb Pasha S/o Althaf @
Syed Althaf, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
(SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.7611/2023 On 12.07.2023 at about 07.30 a.m, the deceased Aqeeb @ Aqeeb Pasha was returning from Imam's house after reading Quran by walking towards his house at Madanagondahalli Road, at that time Mr.Mohammed Thousif Pasha who came on Bajaj Discover Bike bearing No.KA-05-HS-5926 and pickup him to drop and the deceased was pillion rider and said Thousif Pasha was riding the Bike in rash and negligent manner, when they reached Gopalappa's land, near Banniyan Tree, Kasaba Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk, the end of the road in order to take turn, suddenly applied brake and lost control over the vehicle and skid and fell down along with the bike.
Due to this, both rider and pillion rider sustained grievous injuries.
In particular the deceased sustained injuries to head, leg and all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government hospital, Doddaballapura, wherein after first aid he was shifted to NIMHANS hospital, Bengaluru.
But he was succumbed to the injuries on the way to hospital.
The duty doctors examined him and declared brought dead.

The petitioners have spent Rs.1,00,000/-
towards funeral and obsequies ceremonies.
Prior to accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 16 years and was student.
He was the last (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.7611/2023 hope of the petitioners and they were depending upon him for their future life.
The petitioner No.1 being father and petitioner No.2 being mother
have lost love and affection and their life has become dark and miserable.

The accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending Bike and in this regard the Doddaballapura Rural Police have registered a case against rider of said offending Bike in Crime No.207/2023 for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.

The respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a and costs.
03. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent and hence, was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed objection statement.

04. The respondent No.1 in its objection statement has denied the entire case of the petitioners and contended that the Police have filed Charge sheet against rider J1 and owner A1 of the Motor Cycle Althaf Alias Syed Althaf vs Farooq Pasha on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172036919/
2 U/Sec 180, 181 of MV Act, as the rider was not having DL and owner allowed unlicenced minor person to ride (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.7611/2023 the offending vehicle and using vehicle and admits that this respondent No.2 issued policy of insurance in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of Bajaj Discover Bike bearing No.KA-05-HS-5926 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is limited to the terms and conditions of the policy and further denied age of deceased and expenses incurred by the petitioners and dependency of the petitioners and manner of accident and involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of proper and necessary parties.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exaggerated.
Hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs.

05. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues:-
ISSUES 01.
Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependant of deceased Sri.
Aqeeb Pasha S/o Syed Altaf?

02. Whether petitioner prove that deceased Sri.Aqeeb Pasha S/o Syed Altaf was died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 12.07.2023 at about 7.30 a.m., near Gopalan Land, near Banniyan Tree, Madagondanahalli, Kasaba Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk, due to rash and (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.7611/2023 negligent riding of Bajaj Discover Bike bearing registration No.KA-05-HS-5926 by its rider as alleged in the petition?
03. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?
06. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 is examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 16 documents as Ex.P.1 to 16 and closed his side evidence.
07. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 got examined its Manager Legal as RW.1 and got marked one document as Ex.R.1 and closed its side evidence.
08. Heard both sides.

09. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order  for the following:-

sentences.text: Issue No.1 :- Petitioner No.1 in his affidavit stated that, he is the father and petitioner No.2 is the mother.

To prove the said issue No.1, petitioners produced notarized copies of SSLC marks card,
Aadhaar cards and PAN cards as per Ex.P.11 to 16.
These documents clearly goes to show that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased and in the cross- examination, there is no suggestion that they are not the LR's of the deceased.
Hence based on the said Aadhaar Card, this Tribunal answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:- PW.1 filed affidavit by stating that, due to the negligence of the rider of the Bajaj Discover Bike bearing No.KA-05-HS-5926 accident took place and deceased died in the accident.
But in his cross-examination, he denied that there is no negligence by the rider of the Bike and he denied that due to negligence of deceased, accident took place.
On perusal of the exhibited documents, Ex.P.1 FIR in Crime No.207/2023 registered against the Bike rider for the offences punishable U/s.279, 337, 304-A of IPC.

Ex.P.2 is the complaint which shows that due to (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.7611/2023 rash and negligent riding of Bajaj Discover Bike bearing No.KA-05-HS-5926 by its rider the accident took place in which one Aqeeb @ Aqeeb Pasha was sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the way to hospital.

Ex.P.3 and 4 are the Spot Mahazar and Sketch showing the place of accident at Gopalappa's land, near Banniyan Tree, Kasaba Hobli,
Doddaballapura Taluk, is not disputed.
Ex.P.5 is IMV report which shows involvement of offending Motor Cycle in the accident.
Ex.P.6 is the Inquest panchanama which is not disputed the death has taken place.
Ex.P.7 is the PM report showing cause of death is due to cardiac arrest due to head injury sustained.

Ex.P.8 is the Charge sheet filed against the owner of the bike as A1 and rider of the bike as J1 for the offences punishable U/s.279, 337, 304-A of IPC and Sec.181 and 180 of IMV Act and there is no case against the deceased.
Ex.P.9 is the 133 notice issued to the owner of the bike.

Ex.P.10 is the Reply given by the owner stating that one Mohammed Thousif Pasha S/o Farooq Pasha, aged 15 years was riding the bike at the time of accident and he had no driving licence and the vehicle had valid insurance policy.

These documents clearly goes to show that, due to the rash and negligent riding by the (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.7611/2023 rider of the bike who is minor and had no driving licence, accident took place and deceased sustained injuries and died in the accident.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.3:-
This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Aqeeb @ Aqeeb Pasha, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The PW.1/petitioner No.1 has stated that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 16 years and was student and have spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards funeral and obsequies ceremonies.
On account of untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are put to great mental shock and agony and lost love and affection and financial support.

sentences.text: It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age, avocation and income of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioners have not produced any birth certificate, school records of the deceased to show the exact date of birth of the deceased.
However, they have produced Ex.P.11 SSLC marks card and Ex.P.16 Aadhaar card of deceased.

Even though the said documents are not authenticated documents for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.7611/2023 evidence, said documents can be relied upon and according to which his date of birth is mentioned as 05.01.2007 and 26.04.2007.
The alleged accident occurred on 12.07.2023 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased is 16 years.

Therefore,
this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased is 16 years and was minor as on the date of accident.
14. In the case on hand the death of deceased and alleged accident is not denied.

The only contention of the respondent No.2 is that the deceased rider is a unlicenced minor person at the time of accident, hence, the petitioners are not entitled for any compensation from the Insurance Company.

15. To disprove the case of the petitioners, on behalf of the respondent No.2, its the respondent No.2 got examined its Manager Legal as RW.1 and in his chief-examination he has reiterated the written statement averments.
During the course of cross- examination by the petitioner's counsel he stated that the Police have filed Charge sheet against rider who is minor person at the time of accident.
Hence, Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

The petitioners in order to substantiate their claim against the respondent No.2 Insurance Company, have relied upon the following citations:-
01. MFA No.202104/2014 (MV-D) in a case of The Branch Manager, ICICI Lombard Nibhaye Vadde General Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Pooja and others, which relates to pay and recovery principle.

I have gone through the above said citations relied upon by the petitioners and same is not applicable to the case on hand, because the rider of the offending Bike was minor at the time of accident and driven the same without driving licence.

Therefore, respondent No.1 being the RC Owner of offending vehicle shall pay above said compensation amount of Rs.19,21,418/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a to the petitioners from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
(SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.7611/2023 Accordingly, this Issue is answered partly in the Affirmative.
20. Issue No.4:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.19,21,418/- (Rupees Nineteen lakhs twenty one thousand four hundred and eighteen only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.1 - RC Owner shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
The petitioner No.1 being the father and petitioner No.2 being mother of the deceased were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 50-50, in the award amount together with interest.

On deposit of the award amount with interest, the petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled to get release 70% each of the award through E-payment directly to (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.7611/2023 their account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% each shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their names.
The petitioners are at liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

The petitioner No.1 being the father and petitioner No.2 being mother of the deceased were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 50-50, in the award amount together with interest.

On deposit of the award amount with interest, the petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled to get release 70% each of the award through E-payment directly to (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.7611/2023 their account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% each shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their names.
The petitioners are at liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
